text:
janet: Quick sync — we need to align on long-term geo segmentation for the routing policy work. Product wants a clear launch checklist customers can sign up to, sales needs pricing buckets, infra needs migration windows.

kai: Agreed. Can we sketch the minimum viable segmentation tiers? I'm thinking: region-shard (low isolation), region-isolate (data residency + soft-affinity), and tenant-island (full isolation + dedicated capacity).

prashant: That's a good start. For each tier we should define: SLOs (p99 latency target), max burst throughput, isolation guarantees (no noisy neighbor), and rollback path. Also call out observable handoffs.

liz: From product/customer POV: customers ask for two things — predictable latency and clear data-residency controls. They will tolerate limited throughput for stronger isolation if we make tradeoffs explicit.

kai: Operational constraints: cross-region affinity adds egress costs and complexity for KV caching. We need to decide whether to allow cross-region cache peeking for region-isolate tier. If allowed, document the SLO hit and cost multiplier.

janet: Proposal: launch criteria for a tier = 1) defined policy DSL snippet, 2) telemetry/trace hooks + per-tenant cost estimate, 3) migration playbook with <2hr soft-eviction window, 4) canary on 5 pilot tenants.

prashant: +1, add automated rollback to compatible model variant in the same region as a safety net. Also require chaos tests for slow-link failover.

liz: Sales ask: can we expose a simple UI toggle for "Strong Isolation" vs "Standard" so negotiations are easier? Not full gating but helpful for demos.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary policy rollout started for slice-policy-v1 -> 3 nodes demo (logs: https://ci.redwood/dev/rollouts/112).

kai: Nice. Next steps: janet to draft the policy DSL example and launch checklist; prashant to author the migration playbook template; liz to stub the UI toggle copy for pricing. We'll reconvene Tuesday.

janet: I'll drop a short doc in product/roadmap by EOD Monday and ping engineering for tech review.

liz: Thanks — make sure to include explicit cost multipliers per tier so sales can model ARR impact. :money_with_wings:

prashant: One more note — for tenant-island we should require dedicated capacity contract (Reserved capacity) before migration. Otherwise ops risk is high.

janet: Agreed. Adding to checklist.

kai: Thanks all. Keeping the policy DSL small will make rollout easier. Example snippet suggestion for product doc:

```
policy: {
  tier: "region-isolate",
  affinity: "soft",
  kv_cache: "region-local",
  fallback: "region-compatible-quantized",
  sla_p99_ms: 120
}
```

janet: Perfect. See you Tuesday.
